s1: Walter is ninety-two. Three weeks ago he started a new medicine.
s2: Now his hands shake, and a rash is spreading. Forms are hard. He doesn't want his words sent anywhere. So he says nothing.
s3: His doctor gets ten minutes, every few months. How have you been? Fine. He's forgotten how he felt two months ago. So the months in between stay blank.
s4: The drug company has to watch for side effects. What reaches them is thin, late and unstructured.
s5: What if someone simply checked in, every day, at a time Walter chooses?
s6: Miss one day, and his caregiver and care team are alerted. Miss two, and it escalates. Miss three, and his emergency contacts are told. Nobody goes quiet alone.
s7: SafeSignal. Someone is looking out for you.
